properties.decision:
DECIDED AND DONE 2026-08-09, Anthony's word: \"let's discontinue the content store.\" Supersedes dec:where-content-lives, dec:what-lives-where, dec:content-store-implementation, dec:content-manifest and dec:content-growth-is-bounded-by-what-not-by-size.

⭐ THE EVIDENCE WAS USAGE, MEASURED IN EVERY PROJECT THAT HAS IT — reflow2's own design: no --content-path configured, no .reflow2/content directory, and 0 of 148 Fragments carrying a content_ref. flo2: no content path. dev_storyflow: no content directory. THREE PROJECTS, ZERO USE, on a feature that is built, tested and documented.

HIS ARGUMENT, in his words: the bytes cannot fully live in a repo because it would become a huge object rapidly; dev_storyflow's 700+ documents have been ingested and \"those documents are no longer really needed\"; better to put important design artifacts directly in the git repo in something like a design_artifacts folder; it is another feature that must be maintained; and in flo2 the blob could reach terabytes needing backup, security and per-project separation.

AND AN ARGUMENT NOBODY HAD MADE: dec:where-content-lives settled on a content-addressed store whose blobs are COMMITTED TO GIT. Git is already a content-addressed store. The design was a content-addressed layer inside a content-addressed system, and the dedup and integrity hash it provided were both things git already gives anything committed.

AND A FOUNDING MOTIVATION THAT DID NOT SURVIVE: the store was partly built to make sessions \"stateful\" by holding transcripts. cap:session-memory already rejected that mechanism in its own text — \"a pointer to a 3 MB transcript is a RECEIPT, not documentation: leaning on it recreates the markdown problem one level down.\" Its actual design needs no store: takeaways as first-class graph content, the transcript a Fragment carrying a session UUID. See dec:idea-is-session-context-already-in-the-graph.

WHAT WAS REMOVED: content_put / content_get / content_exists / content_manifest, crates/reflow2-core/src/content.rs, crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/content_tools.rs, the --content-path flag, both test files, and the loop nudge's session-artifacts advisory (which told sessions to content_put a rendering).

⚠️ TWO ACCEPTED REQUIREMENTS ARE NOW UNSATISFIED ON PURPOSE, AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. Both are Anthony's own words from 2026-07-31 and the store was their answer:
  · req:agent-artifacts-are-captured — \"in many sessions, the agent will create artifacts... having all these artifacts automatically stored in the reflow2 blob storage would be great.\"
  · req:sources-are-kept-not-just-parsed — ingest keeps the original corpus documents, so the corpus becomes part of the design rather than an input consumed and discarded.
He was shown both in the impact check and chose to KEEP THEM OPEN AND UNANSWERED rather than drop them or claim a replacement. The design_artifacts folder is the intended answer and is UNBUILT, so recording it as satisfied would be fiction. detect_gaps will now ask about them, and that question is the retirement working rather than a bug.

THREE OTHER REQUIREMENTS EXISTED ONLY BECAUSE THE STORE DID and go quiet with it: req:the-store-is-reachable-from-a-session (a surface for it), req:export-says-what-it-cannot-carry (a warning about pointers the export cannot carry), and req:content-reaches-every-seat. Their statuses are Anthony's to move; nothing was changed on his behalf.

⚠️ AND THE REPLACEMENT RESTS ON THE SCHEMA'S WEAKEST JOIN, stated so it is not discovered later: a design_artifacts folder puts the weight on Artifact.location and Fragment.title, which is the field dev_storyflow filed FOUR defects about on this same day — unvalidated paths, a literal ellipsis matching nothing, title-vs-source ambiguity, and no way to ask \"is this path already in the graph?\". That is an argument for fixing `location` before leaning on it, not against the plan.

RETIRED ON THE RECORD, NOT DELETED (retire-from-design, Path A). The capability, its verifications and its artifacts keep their nodes and their history; the ChangeEvent carrying change_type `deprecation` is the marker, because Capability.status has no terminal value — which is exactly dec:idea-does-a-capability-need-a-cancelled-state, still open and still Anthony's, and this is now its first real instance.
properties.name: The content store is discontinued — built, shipped, correct, and used zero times
properties.rationale:
Recorded as a new Decision rather than by editing the five it supersedes, per dec:reopen-supersedes: an accepted decision is never un-accepted, a later one obsoletes it.

The two unsatisfied requirements are named in the decision itself rather than left to be inferred from a gap report, because \"we removed the thing that answered your stated need\" is the part a later reader most needs and the part a tidy graph would hide.
